desk.title: Quarter {{n}}
desk.idle: Idle cash loses about 1% a quarter.
desk.first: Each quarter one company pitches. Ask up to two questions to see its real numbers, then invest or pass. Tap any company on the board to study it.
desk.checkinBody: Review one of your companies. Do its numbers still support holding it?

judgement.title: Your judgement
judgement.sub: Scores how you decide, not what you earn.
judgement.skillsHint: A skill counts once it has come up.

tips.research: Ask both questions before you invest.
tips.skepticism: Treat big stories and tips as claims to check.
tips.calm: Sell on bad data, not on a falling price.
tips.habits: Keep a cash cushion and avoid needless trades.

judgement.basedOn: Based on {{n}} of 5 skills so far

review.askedTwo: You asked both questions, so you decided with real numbers.
review.askedOne: You asked one question. A second shows more.
review.askedNone: You invested without asking anything. Check the numbers first.
review.boughtDespiteWeak: {{checks}} came back Weak and you invested anyway.
review.readChecks: None of the checks you ran were Weak.
review.missedWeak: You did not look at {{checks}}. It was Weak: asking would have shown it.
review.reasonHeadline: “{{reason}}” is what the company shows off, and this one had Weak checks.
review.reasonHeadlineOk: “{{reason}}” is true, but a headline alone is not enough.
review.reasonCurious: Curiosity is fine, but it is not a reason to put money in.
review.concentrated: {{pct}}% of your invested money is in {{sector}}.
review.diversified: Your money is spread across sectors.
review.bigBet: This was {{pct}}% of your net worth in one company.
review.noCushion: You left only {{r_cash}} in cash. Keep a cushion for surprises.
review.outcomeBuyUp: Since then the price is up {{pct}}%. One result is not proof: luck plays a part.
review.outcomeBuyDown: Since then the price is down {{pct}}%. One result is not proof: luck plays a part.
review.soldOnWarnings: You sold as warning signs showed ({{n}} Weak checks). That is the right reason.
review.panicSold: You sold in a market fall with no warning from the company. A falling price is not a falling business.
review.soldTooSoon: You sold a healthy company fast for a small gain. Time is what makes it grow.
review.sellData: You sold for a reason based on data: “{{reason}}”.
review.sellFeeling: “{{reason}}” is a feeling. Sell on bad data, not on a feeling.
review.sellLockProfit: Taking a profit is fine. A healthy business can keep growing, though.
review.sellNoSignal: Nothing in the numbers showed trouble when you sold.
review.forcedSale: You had to sell at a loss or in a dip. A cash cushion lets you wait.
review.forcedSaleOk: You sold to pay the family emergency. A cash cushion avoids forced sales.
review.fee: The sale cost about {{r_fee}} in fees.
review.outcomeSellFell: Since you sold, the price fell {{pct}}%.
review.outcomeSellRose: Since you sold, the price rose {{pct}}%. You could not know that then.
review.passedWeak: You passed on a company with {{n}} Weak checks. Good call.
review.passedStrong: This company looked healthy. Passing is safe, but idle cash loses about 1% a quarter.
review.passNoAsk: You passed without asking. Asking would have taught you why.
review.passAsked: You asked before deciding, so your pass was informed.
review.passReasonCautionOk: “{{reason}}” was cautious, but the numbers were fine.
review.passReasonFeelingOk: Right call, but “{{reason}}” is a feeling. Back it with a number next time.
review.passReasonFeeling: “{{reason}}” is a feeling, and the numbers were fine.
review.heldWeak: You kept it though {{n}} checks are Weak. Selling on bad data is part of the skill.
review.heldStrong: Every check is Strong. Time does the work.
review.heldMixed: Mixed checks ({{n}} Weak). Holding is reasonable, but keep watching.
